blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew
blocking.issue: The regional relay row is out of line with the finalize rules. Finalize waits only for replicas (voters and non-voters), and a read-only relay is neither. After finalize, the relay feed carries N-format entries: the version-advance entry, migrations, new record types, and a full resync, because every replica truncates its log (rule 3) and the relay's last index then comes before the retained log. A relay still at N-1, which the row calls in policy ('one older'), therefore meets a Control Store version above its binary's and halts under rule 4. Its Region's Nodes then serve detached, with no delivery, Enrollment or revocation, until the relay is upgraded.
blocking.evidence: Skew table: "| Regional Ruralz Control relay, Planned (M4) | The replicas' minor or one older; upgrades after the replicas, before its Nodes | Two minors older; newer than the replicas | Same halt rule; form: OQ-system-overview-16 |". Rule 3: "Once every replica reports N and a 24-hour soak (target) has passed, an operator finalizes". Rule 4: "A replica meeting a Control Store version above its binary's, or an unknown entry type, stops before serving". Control plane and GitOps, Relay feed: "It streams committed entries ... or sends full state when that index precedes the retained log".
blocking.fix: Make relays report their binary version on the relay feed and add them to rule 3: finalize requires every replica and every relay to report N. Change the row's in-policy cell to 'the replicas' minor, or one older only while the Control Store version is N-1', and its upgrade timing to 'after every replica reports N and before finalize'. Add that step to Figure 2 between g and h. Cite the read-only relay that Control plane and GitOps already decided, not only OQ-system-overview-16.

blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew
blocking.issue: Rollback after finalize gives no order for Nodes that have already moved to N, and the documented pieces conflict. Upgrade order moves Nodes to N only after finalize. Rule 5 then restores an N-1 Ruralz Control, which leaves those Nodes 'newer than the Control Store version', outside policy with nothing defined about what they get. Returning them to N-1 first can be blocked: once a post-finalize Revision uses an N-only field, the binary rollback limit refuses the handover and a restarted N-1 Node stays not ready. An operator who follows rule 5 after Node upgrades has no in-policy path.
blocking.evidence: Rule 5: "After it, rollback is `ruralz control restore` of the pre-upgrade backup into an empty N-1 deployment". Upgrade order: "After finalize, Nodes take a Zero-Downtime Upgrade ... from N-1 to N." Skew table: "| Ruralz Control and Ruralz Gateway Nodes | N-1; N once the Control Store version is N | N-2 or older; newer than the Control Store version |". Binary rollback limit: "Once a Revision uses a field above N-1's levels ... a handover to N-1 is refused."
blocking.fix: Add one ordered sentence to rule 5. While still on the N deployment, roll out to every Cluster a Revision without N-only fields and let it reach `complete`, so Last-Known-Good is promoted. Then return every Node to N-1 by handover. Only then restore. Add an exception to the skew table if the procedure instead tolerates N Nodes against a restored N-1 Ruralz Control for the duration of the restore, and name Zero-downtime upgrades and hot reload and High availability and disaster recovery as owners of the steps.

blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew
blocking.issue: Rule 2's 'one commit yields one digest' guarantee, and the Semantic versioning table, allow Revision-changing bug fixes that no schema level gates. A minor may ship a 'bug fix changing a Revision'. Rendering 'at N-1's schema levels and defaults' does not reproduce N-1 output when N's renderer or canonicalizer changed, so N and N-1 leaders still produce different digests for one commit mid-upgrade, and `ruralz bundle push` gets RZ-CFG-027 depending on which binary leads. The same table also conflicts with Versioned surfaces and the Configuration model, which allow golden-corpus exceptions only for deliberate default changes that ship as a new schema level. In `ruralz/v1beta1` and `ruralz/v1`, a digest-changing fix also breaks 'defaults never change'.
blocking.evidence: Semantic versioning: "| Bug fix changing a Revision (with a golden-corpus entry); new feature, ... | No | Yes | Yes |". Rule 2: "It also renders Revisions at N-1's schema levels and defaults, so a commit yields one digest, feasible because each default change is a new schema level". Versioned surfaces: "Every release reproduces the golden corpus byte for byte, except entries recording a deliberate default change". Configuration model, Canonical form and Revision: "every release MUST reproduce it byte for byte, except entries that record such a change. Changing the serialization requires a new format identifier."
blocking.fix: Require every change that alters a digest, whether a default change or a render or canonicalization fix, to ship as a new schema level in `ruralz/v1alpha1`. In `ruralz/v1beta1` and `ruralz/v1` it ships only behind a new opt-in field or a new format identifier. Rendering at a level then reproduces that level's output byte for byte. State that CI runs the golden corpus at every level still inside the skew window. Reword the Semantic versioning row to match, and widen the `ruralz bundle push` skew row from 'no `ruralz/v1alpha1` default changed' to 'no schema level added'.

blocking.issue: Applying `ruralz-crds.yaml` before the chart on every upgrade is not feasible when a release adds a served CRD version. When `ruralz.io/v1beta1` first ships, planned for M3 with `ruralz/v1beta1`, the updated CRD lists it as served while every conversion webhook replica still runs N-1 and cannot convert to it. The API server then fails every request in that version and, if the storage version changes in the same release, every write. The failure lasts through the whole rolling Ruralz Control upgrade. If objects are stored in the new version and the operator then rolls back by restore to N-1 (rule 5), the N-1 webhook cannot read them.
blocking.evidence: Release artifacts: "| Helm chart | `oci://ghcr.io/ravindu-rev/charts/ruralz` at the product version; `ruralz-crds.yaml`, applied before the chart on every upgrade | Kubernetes | Planned (M2) |". Migration tooling: "CRDs serve every served version through Ruralz Control's conversion webhook, Planned (M2), so non-storage versions depend on its availability." Figure 2 has no CRD step.
blocking.fix: Apply a CRD manifest that adds a served version only once every Ruralz Control replica runs N (after node g in Figure 2). Make a version the storage version no earlier than the minor after it is first served, so rollback by restore never meets a stored version that N-1 cannot convert. Removals keep the existing rewrite-and-prune rule. Put this in the Helm chart and CRDs skew row, and hand the procedure to Zero-downtime upgrades and hot reload.

blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew
blocking.issue: The 'alternatively' switch for Quota and Token Budget counters still splits counters. Nodes learn the minimum Node version at different times: over the Control Stream, or not at all while detached (P9). One Node can switch at reset R1 while another learns only after R1 and switches at R2, so for the whole window between R1 and R2 the two write different keys. For monthly Quotas that is up to 2x for a month, not 'None'. For Token Budget it breaks the 'admits only when the remaining budget covers the full reservation' rule (P8, pack 8.9). This is what remains of L1-3.
blocking.evidence: "| Quota and Token Budget counters, alternatively | Once the minimum Node version is N, every Node switches at the next window reset | None (hypothesis) |". OQ-release-versioning-and-compatibility-9: "How do Nodes learn the Cluster's minimum Node version ... (a) A new Control Stream field, operator-set in file mode".
blocking.fix: Drop the alternative for Token Budget, which then uses only the shared-hash-tag path. For Quota, make the signal carry an absolute switch window, published at least one full window ahead, so every Node that has the signal switches at the same boundary. Replace 'None' with the residual bound: up to 2x for one window per Node that has not received the signal by then (hypothesis), owned by Scalability and distributed state.

non_blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew
non_blocking.suggestion: Rule 3: say that the forced snapshot re-serializes every FSM record in N format. If the FSM keeps its own bbolt file and snapshots by copying it, records untouched since N-2 keep old encodings, and 'N decodes only N-1 encodings' fails at the next upgrade.

A commit that reached `complete` in staging before finalize and is promoted to prod after it renders with N defaults that staging never ran. Recommend re-rolling the source Environment after finalize, or gating promotion on the schema level the source Revision was rendered at (Configuration model to own).
